questions.q: Which country is traditionally the home of pizza?
questions.x: Modern pizza took shape in Naples, where flatbreads with tomato became a cheap street food in the 1700s and 1800s.

questions.q: Which country is sushi traditionally associated with?
questions.x: The word sushi refers to the vinegared rice, not the fish. The dish began as a way of preserving fish in fermented rice.

questions.q: What fruit is the main ingredient of guacamole?
questions.x: The name comes from the Aztec Nahuatl word ahuacamolli, which roughly means 'avocado sauce'.

questions.q: Which fruit is dried to make raisins?
questions.x: Raisins are traditionally sun-dried. Sultanas and currants are also dried grapes, just of different varieties.

questions.q: What is tofu made from?
questions.x: Tofu is made by curdling soy milk and pressing the curds into blocks, much like making cheese.

questions.q: Which country is feta cheese traditionally from?
questions.x: Traditional feta is brined and made mostly from sheep's milk, sometimes mixed with goat's milk.

questions.q: What sweet food do bees make from flower nectar?
questions.x: Bees fan the nectar with their wings to evaporate water, and enzymes turn it into honey stored in the comb.

questions.q: Which legume is the main ingredient in hummus?
questions.x: Hummus is the Arabic word for chickpeas. The dip is blended with tahini, lemon juice and garlic.

questions.q: Which costly spice consists of the dried stigmas of a crocus flower?
questions.x: Each crocus flower gives just three stigmas, all picked by hand, which is why saffron is so expensive.

questions.q: Which Italian dish layers flat pasta sheets with meat sauce and bechamel?
questions.x: The word lasagna may come from the Greek lasanon, meaning a cooking pot, or from the Latin lasanum.

questions.q: Which nut is the main ingredient of marzipan?
questions.x: Marzipan is a paste of ground almonds and sugar, often shaped into tiny fruits or used to cover cakes.

questions.q: Which country is the long, thin baguette a symbol of?
questions.x: A French decree in 1993 set rules for the 'traditional baguette': only flour, water, salt and yeast.

questions.q: Which gas, made by yeast, makes bread dough rise?
questions.x: Yeast ferments sugars in the dough and releases carbon dioxide, which gets trapped in the gluten and puffs up the loaf.

questions.q: Which vegetable is fermented to make sauerkraut?
questions.x: Sauerkraut means 'sour cabbage' in German. Sailors ate it on long voyages because it kept well.

questions.q: What is the dried seaweed sheet used to wrap sushi rolls called?
questions.x: Nori is made by shredding red algae and pressing it into sheets, much like making paper, then toasting it.

questions.q: Which seeds are roasted and ground to make chocolate?
questions.x: Cacao beans are the seeds of a fruit that grows straight from the trunk and branches of the cacao tree.

questions.q: What is the Italian word for ice cream?
questions.x: Gelato is churned slowly, so it holds less air than American ice cream, and is served a little warmer.

questions.q: Which vegetable is famous for making eyes water when it is cut?
questions.x: Cutting an onion releases a sulfur gas that reacts with the moisture in your eyes and irritates them.

questions.q: Which grain is the staple food of much of Asia?
questions.x: Rice has been farmed for thousands of years, and in many Asian languages the word for rice also means 'meal'.

questions.q: Which country is the traditional home of kimchi?
questions.x: Kimchi is fermented vegetables, most often napa cabbage, seasoned with chili, garlic and ginger.

questions.q: Which kitchen tool is commonly used to flip pancakes?
questions.x: A thin, flexible spatula slides under delicate foods without tearing them.

questions.q: Which kitchen tool do you use to drain boiled pasta?
questions.x: A colander is a bowl full of holes. The word comes from the Latin colare, meaning 'to strain'.

questions.q: Which tool is used to roll dough out flat?
questions.x: Rolling pins can be wood, marble, glass or steel. Some bakers even chill them for flakier pastry.

questions.q: Which vegetable are French fries made from?
questions.x: Belgians and French both claim the fry. In the United States they are called French fries, in Britain they are chips.

questions.q: Which fruit wears its seeds on the outside of its skin?
questions.x: A strawberry has roughly 200 tiny seeds on its surface. Each one is really a separate little fruit.

questions.q: Which Mexican flatbread is made from corn or wheat flour?
questions.x: Corn tortillas date back to the Aztecs and earlier, who made the dough from corn treated with lime.

questions.q: Which Indian flatbread is traditionally baked in a clay oven called a tandoor?
questions.x: Naan dough is stuck to the hot wall of the tandoor, where it puffs up and blisters in minutes.

questions.q: Which Spanish rice dish is traditionally colored and flavored with saffron?
questions.x: The word paella also names the wide, shallow pan the dish is cooked in over an open fire.

questions.q: Which creamy Italian rice dish is stirred slowly while hot broth is added?
questions.x: Risotto rice releases starch as it is stirred, which gives the dish its creamy texture without any cream.

questions.q: Which popular drink comes from steeping leaves in hot water and is often served with lemon?
questions.x: After water, tea is said to be the most widely drunk beverage in the world.

questions.q: Which country is famous for maple syrup and has a maple leaf on its flag?
questions.x: Maple sap is boiled until most of its water has evaporated. Quebec is the biggest syrup-making region.

questions.q: Which herb is the main ingredient in Genoese pesto?
questions.x: Classic pesto also contains pine nuts, garlic, olive oil and hard cheese, crushed together in a mortar.

questions.q: Which cheese is traditionally melted on a Margherita pizza?
questions.x: Mozzarella is a stretchy cheese. Its name comes from the Italian verb mozzare, meaning 'to cut off'.

questions.q: Which meat is traditionally used to make bacon?
questions.x: Bacon is usually cut from the belly or back of a pig and then cured with salt and often smoked.

questions.q: Which Japanese noodle soup is topped with sliced pork and a soft egg?
questions.x: Ramen's wheat noodles came to Japan from China. Regional broths include miso, soy sauce and pork bone.

questions.q: Which country is pho, a beef noodle soup, from?
questions.x: Pho is traditionally eaten at breakfast in Vietnam, with fresh herbs, lime and bean sprouts on the side.

questions.q: Which country is the traditional home of the taco?
questions.x: A taco is just a tortilla wrapped around a filling. Tacos al pastor were inspired by Lebanese immigrants' shawarma.

questions.q: Which vitamin are oranges especially well known for?
questions.x: Sailors once carried citrus fruit on long voyages to prevent scurvy, a disease caused by a lack of vitamin C.

questions.q: Which mineral, found in milk and cheese, is important for strong bones?
questions.x: About 99 percent of the body's calcium is stored in the bones and teeth.

questions.q: Which animal does mutton come from?
questions.x: Mutton comes from an adult sheep. Meat from a young sheep is called lamb.

questions.q: What is meat from a young calf called?
questions.x: Veal is paler and more tender than beef. Wiener schnitzel is traditionally made from it.

questions.q: Venison is meat from which animal?
questions.x: The word venison comes from the Latin venari, meaning 'to hunt'.

questions.q: Which fried chickpea ball is a popular street food across the Middle East?
questions.x: Falafel is often stuffed into pita bread with salad and tahini sauce.

questions.q: Which country is traditionally famous for fondue, a pot of melted cheese?
questions.x: The word fondue is French for 'melted'. Diners dip bread cubes on long forks into a shared pot.

questions.q: Edam and Gouda cheeses come from which country?
questions.x: Both cheeses are named after Dutch towns. Edam is usually sold in a ball coated in red wax.

questions.q: What is the yellow center of an egg called?
questions.x: The yolk holds most of an egg's fat and vitamins, while the white is mostly protein and water.

questions.q: Real mozzarella di bufala is made from the milk of which animal?
questions.x: Italian water buffalo milk is richer than cow's milk, which gives the cheese its creamy flavor.

questions.q: Which compound makes chili peppers taste hot?
questions.x: Capsaicin is concentrated in the white ribs inside the pepper, not in the seeds themselves.

questions.q: Vanilla is the seed pod of which type of flower?
questions.x: Vanilla is the only edible fruit that comes from the orchid family, which has more than 25,000 species.

questions.q: Which hot drink is made from ground roasted beans and served as espresso or latte?
questions.x: Coffee beans are really seeds from the cherry-like fruit of the coffee plant.

questions.q: Which Italian coffee drink has equal parts espresso, steamed milk and milk foam?
questions.x: The drink is named after Capuchin friars, whose brown robes resembled the color of the coffee.

questions.q: In Italian cooking, what does 'al dente' mean when applied to pasta?
questions.x: Al dente literally means 'to the tooth'. Pasta cooked this way also digests more slowly than soft pasta.

questions.q: What is it called to cook food gently in liquid just below boiling point?
questions.x: A simmer shows small, slow bubbles at the surface, while a full boil bubbles vigorously.

questions.q: Which tropical fruit is known for its spiky husk and very strong smell?
questions.x: Durian smells so pungent that it is banned from many hotels and public transport in Southeast Asia.

questions.q: Which fruit is filled with ruby-red, juicy seeds called arils?
questions.x: A single pomegranate can hold several hundred arils, each wrapped around one seed.

questions.q: Traditional caviar is the salted roe of which fish?
questions.x: The best-known caviar comes from sturgeon in the Caspian and Black Seas.

questions.q: Which orange root vegetable is rich in beta-carotene?
questions.x: The body turns beta-carotene into vitamin A. Carrots were originally purple or yellow before orange ones were bred.

questions.q: Which Italian dumplings are traditionally made from potato and flour?
questions.x: Gnocchi are boiled until they float to the surface and are served with sauce or butter.

questions.q: Which country is famous for haggis, a savory pudding of sheep offal and oats?
questions.x: Haggis is traditionally served on Burns Night with mashed turnips and potatoes.

questions.q: Which country is known for the classic dish of battered fish and fried potatoes?
questions.x: Fish and chip shops spread across Britain in the 1860s, and the dish became a staple of working-class meals.

questions.q: Which dairy product is made by churning cream?
questions.x: Churning breaks up the fat globules in cream until they clump together, leaving buttermilk behind.

questions.q: Which dairy food is made by fermenting milk with live bacterial cultures?
questions.x: The bacteria turn milk's lactose into lactic acid, which thickens the milk and gives yogurt its tang.

questions.q: Which ingredient makes up the bulk of most bread dough?
questions.x: Bread flour contains more protein than cake flour, which helps build a strong, chewy structure.

questions.q: What spicy green paste is traditionally served with sushi?
questions.x: Much of the wasabi sold abroad is actually horseradish dyed green. Real wasabi is a rare, hard-to-grow plant.

questions.q: Which fermented soybean paste is the base of a famous Japanese soup?
questions.x: Miso is made by fermenting soybeans with salt and a mold called koji, sometimes with rice or barley added.

questions.q: Which golden spice gives curry its yellow color?
questions.x: Turmeric is the root of a plant in the ginger family. Its color comes from a compound called curcumin.

questions.q: In a restaurant kitchen, what is 'mise en place'?
a: Having all ingredients prepared and in place
questions.x: Mise en place is French for 'putting in place'. Chefs prepare everything before cooking starts.

questions.q: Which Italian dessert layers ladyfingers soaked in coffee with mascarpone cream?
questions.x: Tiramisu means 'pick me up' in Italian, a nod to the caffeine in the coffee-soaked cookies.

questions.q: Which fruit, often treated as a vegetable, is the main ingredient of ketchup?
questions.x: Tomatoes are botanically fruits. Early ketchups were made from mushrooms, walnuts or fish instead.

questions.q: Which French pastry is shaped like a crescent and made of buttery layers?
questions.x: The croissant's flaky texture comes from folding butter into the dough again and again, a process called lamination.

questions.q: Which pastry is made of choux dough, filled with cream and topped with icing?
questions.x: Choux pastry puffs up in the oven with no yeast or baking powder, using only steam.

questions.q: Which delicate French sandwich cookie comes in pastel colors and is made with almond flour?
questions.x: A good macaron has a smooth shell and a ruffled edge at its base, called the 'foot'.

questions.q: Which sweet pastry is made of thin phyllo layers, chopped nuts and syrup?
questions.x: Baklava is popular from Greece and Turkey to the Levant, and a good one can have 30 or more layers of phyllo.

questions.q: Which Spanish fried-dough pastry is often dipped in thick hot chocolate?
questions.x: Churros are piped through a star-shaped nozzle, which creates their signature ridges.

questions.q: Which U.S. holiday is traditionally celebrated with roast turkey and pumpkin pie?
questions.x: Thanksgiving is celebrated on the fourth Thursday of November in the United States.

questions.q: At Spain's yearly food-fight festival in Buñol, what do people throw?
questions.x: La Tomatina has taken place on the last Wednesday of August, and trucks bring in over a hundred tons of ripe tomatoes.

questions.q: Which hard Italian cheese is traditionally grated over pasta?
questions.x: Real Parmigiano Reggiano is aged for at least a year and carries a stamp of origin on its rind.

questions.q: Which spice comes from the inner bark of a tree and is rolled into quills?
questions.x: As the bark dries, it curls into the familiar rolled sticks. It has been traded for over 4,000 years.

questions.q: Which tropical fruit is the signature topping on Hawaiian pizza?
questions.x: Despite the name, Hawaiian pizza was invented in Ontario, Canada, by a Greek-born restaurateur in 1962.

questions.q: Which tart red berry is traditionally made into a sauce for roast turkey?
questions.x: Cranberries grow on low vines in bogs, and farmers often flood the bog to harvest them as they float.

questions.q: Which cereal grain is used to make tortilla chips and polenta?
questions.x: Corn is also called maize. It was first domesticated in Mexico thousands of years ago.

questions.q: Which type of lettuce is traditionally used in a Caesar salad?
questions.x: Romaine leaves are sturdy enough to hold up to the thick dressing of a Caesar salad.

questions.q: Which Indian dish layers rice with spiced meat or vegetables?
questions.x: Biryani is cooked slowly, sometimes sealed with dough so the steam stays inside.

questions.q: Which creamy sauce is made by whisking egg yolk and oil together?
questions.x: Mayonnaise is an emulsion, which means tiny droplets of oil are held in suspension by the egg yolk.

questions.q: Which vegetable is pickled to make gherkins?
questions.x: Gherkins are small, bumpy cucumbers. The word comes from a Dutch term for 'little cucumber'.

questions.q: Which leafy green vegetable made Popeye the cartoon sailor strong?
questions.x: Spinach is a leafy vegetable that gets cooked down a lot: a big pile of raw leaves wilts to just a few spoonfuls.

questions.q: Which part of a chicken is the drumstick?
questions.x: Chicken legs have two parts, the drumstick and the thigh, and both are dark meat.

questions.q: Which kitchen tool is used to beat eggs or whip cream?
questions.x: A whisk's wire loops add air to a mixture, which makes it lighter and fluffier.

questions.q: What do Americans call the fresh leaves of the coriander plant?
questions.x: Cilantro is Spanish for coriander. Some people find it tastes like soap because of a genetic trait.

questions.q: What are the individual segments of a garlic bulb called?
questions.x: A bulb of garlic usually holds about ten to twenty cloves wrapped in papery skin.

questions.q: Which fruit comes in varieties such as Granny Smith and Gala?
questions.x: There are thousands of apple varieties worldwide, and they can range from very sweet to very sour.

questions.q: Sushi rice is seasoned with which sour ingredient?
questions.x: Vinegar was originally used to speed up the fermentation of sushi, and now it adds flavor to the rice.

questions.q: Which fast cooking method uses a hot wok and constant tossing of the food?
questions.x: Stir-frying cooks small pieces of food quickly over very high heat, keeping vegetables crisp.

questions.q: Which kitchen tool is used to remove the skin of potatoes and carrots?
questions.x: Swivel-blade vegetable peelers became common in the 1900s, which made kitchen prep much faster.

questions.q: Which natural sugar is found in milk?
questions.x: Lactose is made of two simpler sugars, glucose and galactose, joined together.

questions.q: Which sour yellow citrus fruit is often squeezed over fish?
questions.x: Lemon juice is acidic, so it can brighten flavors and also stops cut apples from turning brown.

questions.q: Which sugary treat is made by spinning heated sugar into fine threads, often sold at fairs?
questions.x: Cotton candy is called candy floss in Britain. A spinning machine forces melted sugar through tiny holes.

questions.q: Which fruit is dried to make prunes?
questions.x: Not every plum can be made into a prune. Only certain firm, high-sugar varieties dry well without fermenting.

questions.q: Which everyday seasoning is harvested by evaporating seawater or mined from underground?
questions.x: Humans have used salt for thousands of years, and it was once so valuable that it was used as money.

questions.q: Which dark, salty condiment is brewed from fermented soybeans and wheat?
questions.x: Soy sauce originated in China more than 2,000 years ago and later became a staple of Japanese cooking.

questions.q: Which Italian pasta shape's name means 'little ears'?
questions.x: Orecchiette come from Puglia in southern Italy and are traditionally shaped by pressing dough with a thumb.

questions.q: Which pasta's name means 'little tongues' in Italian?
questions.x: Linguine are flat but narrower than fettuccine, and they are classically served with seafood or pesto.

questions.q: Which tube-shaped pasta has diagonally cut ends, like a pen nib?
questions.x: The name penne comes from the Italian word for 'quills' or 'feathers'.

questions.q: Which French blue cheese is made from sheep's milk and aged in caves?
questions.x: Roquefort is aged in natural limestone caves in southern France, where a special mold gives it its blue veins.

questions.q: Which soft, white-rind cheese is traditionally made in Normandy, France?
questions.x: Camembert is traditionally sold in a round wooden box, which helped it travel in the 1800s.

questions.q: Which Swiss cheese is famous for the large holes in it?
questions.x: The holes, called eyes, are formed by gas bubbles that bacteria produce while the cheese ripens.

questions.q: Which Mediterranean island is famous for halloumi cheese?
questions.x: Halloumi has a high melting point, so it can be grilled or fried without turning into a puddle.

questions.q: In which English county is the village that gave Cheddar cheese its name?
questions.x: The Cheddar Gorge caves in Somerset were once used to age the cheese at a steady cool temperature.

questions.q: Which fresh Indian cheese is made by curdling hot milk with an acid and pressing it?
questions.x: Paneer does not melt when heated, so it is cubed and cooked in curries such as palak paneer.

questions.q: Which enzyme is traditionally used to curdle milk when making cheese?
questions.x: Rennet traditionally comes from the stomach lining of young calves, though vegetarian substitutes are now common.

questions.q: Dim sum, small dishes served with tea, belongs to which regional Chinese cuisine?
questions.x: In Guangdong the custom of eating dim sum with tea is called yum cha, which means 'drink tea'.

questions.q: Which Hawaiian dish consists of cubed raw fish tossed with soy sauce and sesame oil?
questions.x: Poke means 'to slice or cut' in Hawaiian.

questions.q: Which fermented soybean cake is a traditional food of Indonesia?
questions.x: Tempeh is made by binding cooked soybeans together with a mold, which creates a firm, nutty cake.

questions.q: Which Korean chili paste is fermented and slightly sweet?
questions.x: Gochujang is made from chili powder, glutinous rice, fermented soybeans and salt.

questions.q: Which fiery red chili paste is a staple of Tunisian and North African cooking?
questions.x: Harissa is made from chilies, garlic, olive oil and spices such as caraway and coriander.

questions.q: Which herb is the main ingredient in Argentine chimichurri sauce?
questions.x: Chimichurri is typically made with parsley, garlic, oregano, vinegar and oil, and served over grilled meat.

questions.q: Which spice is the dried flower bud of a tree and is often stuck into baked hams?
questions.x: Cloves contain eugenol, an oil that gives them their strong, warming scent.

questions.q: Which coffee species is generally described as smoother and sweeter than robusta?
questions.x: Arabica plants prefer high altitudes and contain less caffeine than robusta.

questions.q: What is the finely ground powdered green tea used in the Japanese tea ceremony called?
questions.x: For matcha, tea plants are shaded before harvest, which increases their chlorophyll and gives a rich green color.

questions.q: Which citrus oil gives Earl Grey tea its distinctive flavor?
questions.x: Bergamot is a small, pear-shaped citrus fruit grown mostly in southern Italy.

questions.q: Darjeeling tea is grown in the hills of which country?
questions.x: Darjeeling is called the 'champagne of teas' and is grown in the Himalayan foothills of West Bengal.

questions.q: Black, green and oolong teas all come from the leaves of which plant?
questions.x: The difference between the types is how much the leaves are oxidized after picking.

questions.q: Rooibos, a caffeine-free herbal tea, is grown in which country?
questions.x: Rooibos means 'red bush' in Afrikaans and grows naturally in the Cederberg mountains.

questions.q: Bubble tea, with chewy tapioca pearls, was first made in which place?
questions.x: Bubble tea began in Taiwan in the 1980s and quickly spread across the world.

questions.q: What is the fruit of the coffee plant, which holds the coffee seeds, commonly called?
questions.x: Coffee cherries start green and turn red when ripe, and each usually contains two seeds.

questions.q: Which Italian flatbread is dimpled and topped with olive oil and herbs?
questions.x: Focaccia is related to pizza. Its dimples catch the olive oil, which pools there during baking.

questions.q: Which French bread is enriched with butter and eggs, giving it a rich, soft crumb?
questions.x: Because it holds so much butter, brioche dough must be handled cold and is often mixed for a long time.

questions.q: Which protein network gives bread dough its stretch and structure?
questions.x: Kneading dough aligns the gluten strands, which trap the gas made by yeast.

questions.q: Which raising agent needs an acidic ingredient such as buttermilk to work?
questions.x: Baking powder already contains a dry acid, but baking soda needs one to release its bubbles.

questions.q: What baker's term describes the final rise of shaped dough before baking?
questions.x: Bakers test whether dough is proofed by pressing it gently: it should spring back slowly.

questions.q: What is it called to boil vegetables briefly and then plunge them into ice water?
questions.x: The ice bath stops the cooking and helps vegetables keep their bright color.

questions.q: Which knife cut produces thin matchstick-sized strips?
questions.x: A julienne cut typically measures about 3 millimeters thick, though the size varies by recipe.

questions.q: What does the French cooking term 'sous vide' literally mean?
questions.x: In sous vide cooking, food is sealed in a bag and cooked in a precisely heated water bath.

questions.q: Which mixture of flour and fat is used to thicken sauces such as bechamel?
questions.x: A roux can be cooked white, blond or brown, and the darker it gets, the less thickening power it has.

questions.q: Which trio of onion, carrot and celery forms the flavor base of many French dishes?
questions.x: Italian cooks use a similar base called soffritto, and in Spain it is called sofrito.

questions.q: What do chefs call adding liquid to a hot pan to loosen the browned bits stuck to it?
questions.x: Those browned bits, called fond, are packed with flavor and make the base of a pan sauce.

questions.q: A pestle is paired with which kitchen vessel to crush spices?
questions.x: The mortar and pestle is one of the oldest kitchen tools and has been used for thousands of years.

questions.q: Which North African cooking pot has a distinctive cone-shaped lid?
questions.x: The cone lets steam rise, condense and trickle back down, keeping the stew moist as it simmers.

questions.q: Which of these fruits is botanically a berry?
questions.x: Botanists define a berry as a fleshy fruit with seeds inside. Strawberries and raspberries do not qualify.

questions.q: The grapefruit is a natural hybrid of the sweet orange and which other fruit?
questions.x: The grapefruit first appeared in Barbados in the 1700s and got its name from the way it grows in grape-like clusters.

questions.q: Which tropical fruit is the largest that grows on trees?
questions.x: A single jackfruit can weigh over 40 kilograms (about 90 pounds).

questions.q: Which vegetable gives the soup borscht its deep red color?
questions.x: Borscht is eaten across Eastern Europe, and recipes vary widely from town to town.

questions.q: Capers are the pickled version of which part of the caper bush?
questions.x: If the buds are left to bloom and fruit, they become caperberries, which are also pickled.

questions.q: The vanilla orchid is native to which country?
questions.x: Vanilla is native to Mexico, but today Madagascar grows most of the world's vanilla.

questions.q: The Latin name of the cacao tree, Theobroma, means 'food of the what'?
questions.x: The Swedish scientist Carl Linnaeus gave the cacao tree this name in 1753.

questions.q: Which American chef introduced French cooking to U.S. audiences with the TV show 'The French Chef'?
questions.x: Julia Child's cookbook 'Mastering the Art of French Cooking' came out in 1961.

questions.q: Which chef and TV host wrote the 2000 book 'Kitchen Confidential'?
questions.x: The book was a candid look at restaurant kitchens and launched Bourdain's career as a travel and food writer.

questions.q: In which region did potatoes originate before reaching Europe?
questions.x: Farmers in the Andes grew thousands of potato varieties long before Spanish explorers brought them to Europe.

questions.q: Which French scientist gave his name to the heating process that makes milk safer to drink?
questions.x: Pasteur developed the process in the 1860s, first to keep wine from spoiling.

questions.q: Which noodles are traditionally eaten in Japan on New Year's Eve?
questions.x: The tradition is called toshikoshi soba, and the long noodles stand for a long life.

questions.q: The meringue dessert pavlova is named after a famous ballerina from which country?
questions.x: Anna Pavlova toured Australia and New Zealand in the 1920s, and both countries claim the dessert.

questions.q: Which Italian queen is the Margherita pizza traditionally said to be named after?
questions.x: The legend says a Neapolitan pizza maker made a pizza in 1889 with red, white and green toppings to match the flag.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of stars in the Michelin Guide's restaurant rating?
questions.x: Three stars means 'exceptional cuisine, worth a special journey'.

questions.q: The Michelin Guide was first published by a company that made what?
questions.x: The French Michelin brothers started the guide in 1900 to encourage drivers to travel, and so wear out their tires.

questions.q: What is the name of the browning reaction between amino acids and sugars that gives seared steak its flavor?
questions.x: It is named for the French chemist Louis-Camille Maillard, who described it in 1912.

questions.q: Which natural substance in fruit helps jam set into a gel?
questions.x: Apples and citrus peels are rich in pectin, which is why they are often added to jams made from low-pectin fruit.

questions.q: Which gelling agent made from red algae is a vegetarian alternative to gelatin?
questions.x: Agar sets at room temperature and is used widely in Asian desserts.

questions.q: Botanically, peanuts belong to which plant group?
questions.x: Peanut pods develop underground, and the plant is a close relative of peas and beans.

questions.q: Couscous is made from tiny granules of which ingredient?
questions.x: Couscous is a staple of North African cooking and is traditionally steamed over a stew.

questions.q: Shakshuka consists of eggs poached in a sauce of which main ingredients?
questions.x: Shakshuka is popular across North Africa and the Middle East, and it is usually eaten with bread for dipping.

questions.q: Baba ganoush is a smoky dip made mostly from which vegetable?
questions.x: The eggplant is charred over a flame until its skin blackens, which gives the dip its smoky taste.

questions.q: Tahini is a paste made from ground what?
questions.x: Tahini is used in hummus and in the sweet candy halva.

questions.q: Which clarified butter is a staple of Indian cooking?
questions.x: Ghee is made by simmering butter and removing the milk solids, so it can be heated to a high temperature.

questions.q: Which Vietnamese sandwich is served on a baguette-style roll?
questions.x: Banh mi combines French bread with Vietnamese fillings such as pickled carrot, cilantro and chili.

questions.q: Which Indonesian dish is made by frying cooked rice with sweet soy sauce?
questions.x: Nasi goreng means 'fried rice' in Indonesian and Malay and is often topped with a fried egg.

questions.q: Adobo, meat braised in vinegar, soy sauce and garlic, is often called the national dish of which country?
questions.x: Vinegar preserved the meat in the tropical climate before refrigeration existed.

questions.q: Which Chinese city is famous for its crisp, lacquered roast duck?
questions.x: The duck is carved in front of diners and served with thin pancakes, scallions and sweet bean sauce.

questions.q: Bibimbap, a Korean rice bowl, literally means what?
questions.x: The bowl is topped with vegetables, meat and egg, then mixed together with gochujang before eating.

questions.q: Fugu is the Japanese name for which fish whose organs are poisonous if prepared wrongly?
questions.x: In Japan, fugu chefs need special training and a license to prepare the fish.

questions.q: Mochi, a chewy Japanese treat, is made by pounding what?
questions.x: Mochi is traditionally pounded with a wooden mallet in a large mortar, especially around New Year.

questions.q: Feijoada, a stew of black beans and pork, is traditionally considered a national dish of which country?
questions.x: Feijoada is traditionally served with rice, sliced orange and toasted cassava flour.

questions.q: Which Canadian province is the home of poutine, fries topped with cheese curds and gravy?
questions.x: Poutine appeared in rural Quebec in the late 1950s. Fresh cheese curds should squeak when you bite them.

questions.q: Gumbo and jambalaya are signature dishes of which U.S. state?
questions.x: Both dishes blend French, Spanish and West African cooking traditions found in Louisiana.

questions.q: Pesto, the basil and pine nut sauce, comes from which Italian city?
questions.x: The name pesto comes from the Genoese word for 'to pound', a reference to the mortar and pestle.

questions.q: Panettone, the tall sweet bread with candied fruit, is associated with which Italian city?
questions.x: Panettone is traditionally baked at Christmas, and its dough can take more than a day to rise.

questions.q: Which short-grain rice is the classic choice for making risotto?
questions.x: Arborio rice is named for a town in the Piedmont region and is rich in starch.

questions.q: Paella traditionally comes from which Spanish region?
questions.x: The original Valencian paella contained rabbit, chicken and green beans, not seafood.

questions.q: Which French port city is the home of bouillabaisse fish stew?
questions.x: Bouillabaisse started as a humble stew that fishermen made from the bony fish they could not sell.

questions.q: Which region of northeastern France gave its name to a savory egg-and-bacon tart?
questions.x: The name quiche comes from the German word Kuchen, meaning 'cake'.

questions.q: What kind of organism is a truffle?
questions.x: Truffles grow underground near tree roots and are traditionally found with the help of trained dogs or pigs.

questions.q: Which spice defines the flavor and red color of Hungarian goulash?
questions.x: Hungary grows many varieties of paprika, from sweet to hot.

questions.q: Traditional Wiener schnitzel from Vienna is made from which meat?
questions.x: In Austria, a schnitzel must be made from veal to be called 'Wiener' schnitzel.

questions.q: In Spain, what is a tortilla espanola made from?
questions.x: Unlike a Mexican tortilla, the Spanish version is a thick omelet that is often served in slices as tapas.

questions.q: Which pastry is traditionally eaten during China's Mid-Autumn Festival?
questions.x: Mooncakes are often filled with lotus seed paste and a salted egg yolk that represents the full moon.

questions.q: Macadamia nuts are native to which country?
questions.x: Macadamias grew wild in the rainforests of eastern Australia before Hawaii began growing them in the 1800s.

questions.q: What do Britons call a zucchini?
questions.x: Courgette comes from French. The two names describe the same vegetable.

questions.q: In most of the world outside North America, what is corn usually called?
questions.x: Maize comes from the Taino word mahiz. In Britain, 'corn' once meant any cereal grain.

questions.q: Bay leaves come from which tree?
questions.x: Bay laurel leaves flavor soups and stews, and are removed before serving because they stay tough.

questions.q: Paprika is made by grinding dried what?
questions.x: Paprika comes in sweet, hot and smoked varieties, depending on the peppers used.

questions.q: Which part of the ginger plant do we eat?
questions.x: A rhizome is an underground stem, which looks like a root.

questions.q: Which dark, sticky syrup is a by-product of refining sugar?
questions.x: Blackstrap molasses is what is left after the third boiling of sugar cane juice.

questions.q: What does the Scoville scale measure?
questions.x: The scale is named for the American pharmacist Wilbur Scoville, who devised it in 1912.

questions.q: Which vitamin does the body make when skin is exposed to sunlight?
questions.x: Vitamin D also occurs in a few foods such as egg yolks and oily fish.

questions.q: Which mineral, abundant in bananas, helps nerves and muscles function?
questions.x: Potassium is also plentiful in potatoes, beans and avocados.

questions.q: Which compound gives black pepper its sharp bite?
questions.x: The name of the compound comes from Piper nigrum, the Latin name of the pepper vine.

questions.q: What is the thin outer colored layer of citrus peel, grated for flavor, called?
questions.x: The white layer just below the zest is the pith, which tastes bitter and is usually avoided.

questions.q: Which cold tomato soup is a specialty of Andalusia in southern Spain?
questions.x: Gazpacho is blended raw vegetables, olive oil and vinegar, and is often served on hot summer days.

questions.q: Which type of cookware needs a layer of baked-on oil, called seasoning, to stay non-stick?
questions.x: With care, a seasoned cast-iron pan can last for generations and be handed down in families.

questions.q: The mango is native to which region of the world?
questions.x: Mangoes have been grown in India for thousands of years, and the mango is that country's national fruit.

questions.q: Braising combines which two cooking methods?
a: Searing, then slow cooking in liquid
questions.x: Braising turns tough cuts of meat tender, as the connective tissue melts in the hot liquid.

questions.q: Which French chef, known as the 'king of chefs', organized professional kitchens into the brigade system?
questions.x: Escoffier's brigade divided a kitchen into stations such as saucier and patissier, a model still used today.

questions.q: Which Japanese chemist identified umami as a basic taste in 1908?
questions.x: Ikeda isolated glutamate from kombu seaweed broth, which led to the invention of MSG.

questions.q: Which Frenchman developed the method of preserving food in sealed containers, a forerunner of canning?
questions.x: Appert won a prize offered by Napoleon's government for a way to feed armies, and he published his method in 1810.

questions.q: For which Australian soprano did Escoffier create a dessert of peaches and vanilla ice cream?
questions.x: Melba toast is also named after her, as she ate thin crisp toast while she was ill.

questions.q: Which Italian-born restaurateur is credited with inventing the famous salad of romaine, croutons and Parmesan in 1920s Tijuana?
questions.x: Cardini ran a restaurant in Tijuana, Mexico, and the salad was named after him, not after Julius Caesar.

questions.q: What is the minimum aging time for authentic Parmigiano Reggiano?
questions.x: Many wheels are aged for two years or more, which gives them a crumbly texture and crunchy crystals.

questions.q: Manchego cheese is traditionally made from the milk of which animal?
questions.x: The cheese comes from the La Mancha region of Spain, and its pattern on the rind recalls the grass molds once used.

questions.q: According to legend, which Ethiopian goat herder discovered coffee?
questions.x: The tale says Kaldi noticed his goats dancing with energy after eating red berries from a certain shrub.

questions.q: Which ethnic group of Sumatra is traditionally credited with creating the slow-cooked dish rendang?
questions.x: Rendang is simmered in coconut milk and spices until the liquid cooks away and the meat turns dark and dry.

questions.q: The Japanese santoku kitchen knife's name is usually translated as what?
questions.x: The three virtues refer to its ability to slice, dice and mince, or to handle meat, fish and vegetables.

questions.q: Which French magistrate wrote the 1825 book 'The Physiology of Taste'?
questions.x: Brillat-Savarin is famous for the line 'Tell me what you eat, and I will tell you what you are'.

questions.q: Which classic French sauce is made from brown stock and a brown roux?
questions.x: Espagnole is the base for demi-glace, which chefs make by simmering it with more brown stock until it reduces.

questions.q: Which compound is responsible for the tingling, numbing sensation of Sichuan peppercorns?
questions.x: Sichuan peppercorns are not related to black pepper or chilies, and in Chinese they are called huajiao.

questions.q: Which sulfur compound forms when garlic cloves are crushed or chopped?
questions.x: Allicin gives fresh garlic its sharp smell and forms when two substances inside the clove meet after cutting.

questions.q: Which substance in egg yolk helps oil and water blend together in mayonnaise?
questions.x: Lecithin molecules have one end that likes water and another that likes oil, so they hold the two together.

questions.q: What is the process of soaking corn in limewater called, which makes tortillas easier to make and more nutritious?
questions.x: The process dates back to ancient Mesoamerica and frees the niacin in corn, which the body could not otherwise absorb easily.

questions.q: Which Spanish chef led the influential elBulli restaurant, known for molecular gastronomy?
questions.x: ElBulli sat on the Costa Brava and closed in 2011, after Adria had made foams and edible spheres famous.

questions.q: What was the fermented fish sauce that ancient Romans used as a staple seasoning?
questions.x: Garum was made by salting fish guts and leaving them in the sun, and it was a major trade product.

questions.q: The oldest surviving Roman cookbook, 'De re coquinaria', is traditionally attributed to whom?
questions.x: The recipes call for lots of garum and spices, including pepper, which was imported from India.

questions.q: The word 'ketchup' is thought to come from a Hokkien Chinese word for what kind of sauce?
questions.x: The word ke-tsiap referred to a fermented fish brine, which British sailors brought home and adapted.

questions.q: Which salty little fish is a key ingredient of Worcestershire sauce?
questions.x: The sauce is aged in barrels for months, which mellows the fishy flavor into a savory depth.

questions.q: Which Louisiana island is the home of Tabasco hot sauce?
questions.x: The McIlhenny family has made the sauce on the island since the 1860s and ages the pepper mash in barrels.

questions.q: Sriracha sauce is named after a coastal town in which country?
questions.x: Si Racha is a port town on the Gulf of Thailand, and the sauce first became popular locally as a dip for seafood.

questions.q: What is the Japanese name for the pickled ginger served with sushi?
questions.x: Gari is eaten between pieces of sushi to refresh the palate.

questions.q: Which dried fermented tuna relative is shaved to flavor Japanese dashi broth?
questions.x: A block of katsuobushi is as hard as wood and is shaved into thin, aromatic flakes.

questions.q: Which European country's traders are traditionally credited with introducing tempura-style frying to Japan?
questions.x: The word tempura may come from the Portuguese tempero, meaning seasoning, or from 'Ember Days' fasting times.

questions.q: Nutmeg and mace come from trees native to which Indonesian islands?
questions.x: The Dutch fought bitterly for control of the Banda Islands in the 1600s to hold the nutmeg monopoly.

questions.q: Which country is the source of 'true' cinnamon, Cinnamomum verum?
questions.x: Sri Lankan cinnamon is lighter and more delicate than the cassia cinnamon sold in most supermarkets.

questions.q: Who, as a 12-year-old in 1841, devised the hand-pollination method that made vanilla farming practical outside Mexico?
questions.x: Albius lived on Reunion Island, and his method is still used on vanilla farms today.

questions.q: Which Swiss chocolatier invented milk chocolate in 1875?
questions.x: Peter used the condensed milk invented by his neighbor Henri Nestle to make the first milk chocolate.

questions.q: Which Yemeni port city gave its name to a coffee-and-chocolate flavor?
questions.x: Mocha was once the world's chief port for the coffee trade, long before coffee was grown elsewhere.

questions.q: Pu-erh, a fermented tea pressed into cakes, comes from which Chinese province?
questions.x: Pu-erh is pressed into cakes that can be aged for decades.

questions.q: Which duchess is credited with popularizing afternoon tea in England in the 1840s?
questions.x: She felt hungry in the late afternoon, since dinner was served late, and began having tea and snacks in her room.

questions.q: In the 1893 case Nix v. Hedden, what did the U.S. Supreme Court classify the tomato as for tariff purposes?
questions.x: Botanically it is a fruit, but the court ruled that in common usage it was served with dinner like a vegetable.

questions.q: The kiwifruit was originally marketed under what name before it was renamed for export?
questions.x: New Zealand exporters renamed the fruit after their national bird, the kiwi, in the 1950s.

questions.q: Which banana variety dominated world exports until Panama disease devastated it in the mid-1900s?
questions.x: The Cavendish banana replaced it because it resisted the disease.

questions.q: The wild ancestor of the domestic apple grows in the mountains of which country?
questions.x: Malus sieversii still grows in the Tian Shan range, and the Kazakh city of Almaty means 'father of apples'.

questions.q: Himalayan pink salt is mined mainly in which country?
questions.x: The salt comes from the Khewra mine, which is one of the biggest salt mines in the world.

questions.q: About how many gallons of maple sap are boiled down to make one gallon of syrup?
questions.x: The sap is only about 2 percent sugar, so most of the water has to boil off.

questions.q: Which famous New York hotel gave its name to a salad of apples, celery, grapes and walnuts?
questions.x: Oscar Tschirky, the hotel's maitre d', introduced the salad in the 1890s.

questions.q: Which cured pork cheek is the traditional meat in authentic spaghetti carbonara?
questions.x: Guanciale has more fat than bacon and gives the sauce a richer flavor than other cured pork.

questions.q: What do the Iberian pigs behind the finest jamon iberico de bellota feast on?
questions.x: Bellota is Spanish for acorn. The pigs roam oak woodlands and can eat over 10 kilograms a day.

questions.q: Cassoulet, a slow-baked casserole of white beans, sausage and duck, comes from which French region?
questions.x: The dish is named after the cassole, the clay pot it is cooked in.

questions.q: Which region of France is famous for buckwheat galettes and sweet crepes?
questions.x: Buckwheat grows well in Brittany's poor soil, which is why savory galettes became the local staple.

questions.q: Ratatouille, the vegetable stew, originated in which region of France?
questions.x: Ratatouille contains summer vegetables, such as tomatoes, eggplant, zucchini and peppers.

questions.q: Traditional Irish soda bread rises thanks to baking soda reacting with which tangy ingredient?
questions.x: The recipe developed in 19th-century Ireland, where soft wheat flour was low in gluten and bakers wanted a quick bread without yeast.

questions.q: The Sachertorte, a famous chocolate cake with apricot jam, comes from which city?
questions.x: The cake was created in 1832 by Franz Sacher, a 16-year-old apprentice, for Prince Metternich.

questions.q: Pasteis de nata, Portugal's custard tarts, are most closely linked to which Lisbon district?
questions.x: Monks at the Jeronimos Monastery in Belem began selling the tarts in the early 1800s.

questions.q: Australian lamingtons are sponge cakes coated in chocolate and rolled in what?
questions.x: The cake is thought to be named after Lord Lamington, a Governor of Queensland in the late 1800s.

questions.q: West African fufu is traditionally made by pounding which starchy ingredients?
questions.x: Fufu is rolled into a ball and used to scoop up soups and stews.

questions.q: Dosa, the South Indian crepe, is made from a fermented batter of rice and which lentil?
questions.x: The batter ferments overnight, making the dosa tangy and crisp.

questions.q: Mapo tofu, a spicy dish of tofu with ground meat, comes from which Chinese province?
questions.x: The dish is thought to have been created in the 1800s in Chengdu, and it has a tingly, numbing heat.

questions.q: Takoyaki, the octopus-filled batter balls, are a street food from which Japanese city?
questions.x: Takoyaki are cooked in a special pan with half-sphere molds and turned with picks.

questions.q: Which tart red spice is a key ingredient in the Middle Eastern blend za'atar?
questions.x: Sumac comes from the dried berries of a shrub and gives a lemony tang.

questions.q: The name of the Italian cheese ricotta means what?
questions.x: Ricotta is made by heating the whey left over from making other cheeses a second time.

questions.q: What baking term describes resting flour and water together before adding salt and yeast?
questions.x: The technique was popularized by French bakery expert Raymond Calvel and improves dough structure.

questions.q: Which pre-ferment of equal parts flour and water, traditionally linked to Poland, is used in baguettes?
questions.x: Viennese bakers brought the method to Paris in the 1800s, and it gives bread a nutty flavor and open crumb.

questions.q: Which spice is a typical part of Chinese five-spice powder, along with star anise, cloves, cinnamon and fennel?
questions.x: The five-spice blend is meant to balance the five flavors of sweet, sour, bitter, pungent and salty.

questions.q: Which anise-scented herb is a defining flavor of sauce bearnaise?
questions.x: Bearnaise is hollandaise with a reduction of vinegar, shallots and tarragon, and it is classic with steak.

questions.q: Broccoli, cabbage and kale are all cultivated forms of which wild plant?
questions.x: Farmers bred the same species into different shapes, which is why they are all Brassica oleracea.

questions.q: Globe artichokes are the unopened flower buds of what kind of plant?
questions.x: If left on the plant, the bud blooms into a large purple flower.

questions.q: The cashew tree is native to which country?
questions.x: Portuguese traders carried cashews from Brazil to India and Africa in the 1500s.

questions.q: Which French chef, nicknamed 'the king of chefs and chef of kings', cooked for Napoleon's circle and the British Prince Regent?
questions.x: Careme was a pioneer of haute cuisine and designed towering pastry centerpieces.

questions.q: In which California city is Alice Waters' influential restaurant Chez Panisse?
questions.x: Chez Panisse opened in 1971 and helped launch the movement for local, seasonal ingredients.

questions.q: Which Danish city is home to the restaurant Noma, co-founded by chef Rene Redzepi?
questions.x: Noma helped shape the New Nordic movement, which focuses on local and foraged ingredients.

questions.q: Which Victorian author published 'The Book of Household Management' in 1861?
questions.x: Mrs Beeton's book was a bestseller, giving advice on cooking, servants and household budgets.

questions.q: The Italian town of Ivrea is famous for an annual battle in which people throw what?
questions.x: The Battle of the Oranges is part of the Carnival of Ivrea, with teams on foot attacking carts.

questions.q: In which English county is the annual cheese-rolling event at Cooper's Hill held?
questions.x: Competitors chase a wheel of Double Gloucester cheese down a steep hillside, and the first to the bottom wins it.

questions.q: The town of Alba, famous for its white truffle fair, is in which Italian region?
questions.x: White truffles from the Alba area are among the most prized foods and cannot be farmed.

questions.q: The Microplane grater began life as what kind of tool?
questions.x: A home cook reportedly grated citrus zest with one of the woodworking tools, and the company then marketed it for kitchens.

questions.q: Which French physicist invented an early pressure cooker, called the 'steam digester', in 1679?
questions.x: Papin's invention raised water's boiling point by trapping steam, which cooked food faster and softened bones.

questions.q: The knife cut 'brunoise' produces what?
questions.x: A brunoise is made by cutting julienne strips crosswise into tiny cubes.

questions.q: A duck confit is meat that has been slowly cooked in what?
questions.x: Confit is an old preservation method, as the meat was stored under a layer of fat that sealed out air.

questions.q: The French cooking term 'saute' literally means what?
questions.x: It refers to how food jumps in a hot pan as it is tossed.

questions.q: Which process of heating and cooling chocolate gives it a glossy shine and a crisp snap?
questions.x: Tempering aligns the fat crystals in cocoa butter into a stable form, so the bar does not turn dull or crumbly.

questions.q: A bain-marie is used in cooking to do what?
a: Heat food gently in a water bath
questions.x: Setting a bowl over simmering water keeps delicate sauces and chocolate from scorching.

questions.q: Which vitamin, abundant in leafy greens, is needed for blood to clot?
questions.x: The K comes from the German word Koagulation, and the vitamin is found in kale, spinach and broccoli.

questions.q: Which B vitamin is found naturally almost only in animal products?
questions.x: People who follow plant-based diets usually get B12 from fortified foods.

questions.q: Mozzarella belongs to the 'pasta filata' family of cheeses. What does pasta filata mean?
questions.x: The curd is heated and stretched like taffy, which gives these cheeses their stringy texture.

questions.q: Kobe beef takes its name from a city in which Japanese prefecture?
questions.x: Kobe beef comes from Tajima-gyu cattle, a strain of Wagyu raised in Hyogo Prefecture.

questions.q: The Maori earth oven, where food is cooked with heated stones underground, is called what?
questions.x: Food is wrapped and lowered onto hot stones, then covered with soil and left to steam for hours.

questions.q: Bobotie, a baked dish of spiced minced meat with an egg topping, is a classic of which country?
questions.x: Bobotie draws on Cape Malay cooking, and it is traditionally served with yellow rice.

questions.q: Smorrebrod, the open-faced sandwich on rye bread, is a classic of which country?
questions.x: Danish smorrebrod are piled with toppings like herring, roast beef and egg, and eaten with a knife and fork.

questions.q: Black pepper is native to the Malabar Coast of which country?
questions.x: Pepper was once so valuable in Europe that it was sometimes counted peppercorn by peppercorn as currency.

questions.q: Traditional balsamic vinegar of Modena is made by slowly cooking down the juice of which fruit?
questions.x: The cooked grape must is aged for at least 12 years in a series of barrels made of different woods.

questions.q: Which grain is used to make the Ethiopian flatbread injera?
questions.x: Teff is one of the world's smallest grains, and injera batter is fermented for several days.

questions.q: Which compound gives saffron its golden-yellow color?
questions.x: Crocin is a water-soluble pigment, which is why saffron threads turn a dish yellow when steeped.

questions.q: What is a smoke-dried jalapeno pepper called?
questions.x: Chipotle comes from the Nahuatl word for smoked chili, and the peppers are often sold in adobo sauce.

questions.q: Which grain is traditionally used to make Scandinavian knackebrod crispbread?
questions.x: Rye grows well in cool northern climates, and crispbread keeps for months without going stale.

questions.q: In which decade was the Italian ciabatta loaf developed?
questions.x: A baker from the Veneto region created ciabatta in 1982 as an Italian answer to the French baguette.

questions.q: Which Austrian crescent-shaped pastry is traditionally seen as an ancestor of the croissant?
questions.x: Kipferl had existed in Austria for centuries before it reached France and was reinvented with laminated dough.

questions.q: The French word 'eclair' literally means what?
questions.x: One theory says the pastry is so delicious that it vanishes as fast as a flash of lightning.

questions.q: Which cracked wheat is the main grain in tabbouleh?
questions.x: Tabbouleh originated in the mountains of Lebanon and Syria and is mostly parsley, with a little bulgur.

questions.q: In which animal's stomach is haggis traditionally boiled?
questions.x: Modern haggis is often cooked in an artificial casing instead.

questions.q: Currywurst, sausage with curry-flavored ketchup, is a famous street food from which German city?
questions.x: Herta Heuwer is said to have invented currywurst in Berlin in 1949, using ingredients from British soldiers.

questions.q: Tahdig is the prized crispy layer formed at the bottom of a pot of what in Persian cooking?
questions.x: Tahdig means 'bottom of the pot' in Persian and is often served flipped out in one golden piece.

questions.q: Mastic, a resin used to flavor Greek sweets and chewing gum, comes from trees on which Greek island?
questions.x: Mastic trees grow in southern Chios, and the resin is collected from cuts in the bark, drying into small tears.

questions.q: Which French novelist's memory of dipping a madeleine into tea sparked a famous book series?
questions.x: The scene appears in 'In Search of Lost Time', where the taste of the cake brings back childhood memories.

questions.q: The cheese dish raclette takes its name from a French verb meaning what?
questions.x: A half wheel of cheese is melted near heat and the soft layer is scraped onto potatoes.

questions.q: The Turkish word 'dolma' refers to foods that are what?
questions.x: Dolma are vegetables or leaves, such as grape leaves and peppers, filled with rice, herbs or meat.
